At 17:39:41 UT on 13 Oct 2025 FERMI GBM detect Long GRB 251013C [GCN 42221]. At 2025-10-13T17:39:42 UTC SVOM/ECLAIRs also detected GRB 251013C and after 203 s SVOM/MXT began to observe [GCN 42222]. 6.85 minutes later t0 SVOM/VT deteced OT at R.A., Dec. 345.8356, -0.2103 degrees with an uncertainty of 0.5 arcsec [GCN 42223]. BOOTES-6, LAST, NOT, LCO,SAO RAS Zeiss-1000, GOTO, SLKT, DDOTI,COLIBRI, SYSU, ABO, Asiago, NUTTelA, BBO, OHP/T193, MerSEC, OANV, Calapai Observatory, MAO/AZT-22, KNC, JinShan, Leavitt Observatory and Liverpool 2-m t telscopes also detected afterglow of the GRB251013C
Redshidt z = 0.572 found by NOT [GCN 42227].

Long GRB 250424A was detected by **SWIFT/BAT** at 2025-04-24T06:52:28.51 UT. It is a long GRB (T90=19s in the 15-350 keV), GCN 40224. The GRB was independently detected by other experiments as **CZT** measures T90 of 9.2 (+1.5 -1.0) s in the 20-200 keV (GCN 40231), **Astrosat/CSi** measures a T90 of 14 (+1, -3) s in 100-500 keV (GCN 40231), **Konus-Wind** on 2025-04-24T06:52:13.431 with a duration of about 40.5 s in the 20 keV - 10 MeV (GCN 40243), **EIRSAT-1** on 2025-04-24T06:52:12.6 (GCN 40249), **SVOM/GRM** on 2025-04-24T06:52:08 with a T90 of 18.8 +1.0/-1.0 s in the 15-5000 keV (GCN 40252), **CGBM** on 2025-04-24T06:52:04.323 with T90 = 13.5 +/- 0.8 s in 40-1000 keV (GCN 40298).  T0 is defined as the **SVOM/GRM** trigger.The X-ray counterpart was found by **Swift/XRT** (GCN 40224, 40233, 40232) and was enhanced the position (using the **XRT-UVOT** alignment): RA, Dec = 217.49920, -35.02504 (GCN 40232). An optical follow-up campaign was performed including **MASTER-OAFA** (GCN 40222), **SWIFT/UVOT** (GCN 40224, 40244), **REM** (GCN 40225, including NIR afterglow), **DDOTI** (GCN 40226), **VLT** (GCN 40228), **BlackGEM** (GCN 40229), **COLIBRÍ** (GCN 40230), **Skynet** (GCN 40241), **SVOM/VT** (GCN 40246), **LCO** (GCN 40263). A NIR observation campaign was performed including **REM** (GCN 40225), **WINTER** (GCN 40250), **PRIME** (GCN 40251). The Redshift estimated in GCN Circular 40228 (**VLT/X-shooter**). The host galaxy proposed in GCN Circular 40227 was also identified. The GRB have possibility to be a supernova as GCN 40461 reported. The coordinates of the Skyportal page of the ones provided by the detection of the afterglow optical counterpart of Swift/UVOT (GCN 40224).
GRANDMA and KNC (GCN 40240, GCN 40920) also responded to the alert.

Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) detected a 5s relatively short-duration GRB at 21-02-2025 03:34:37 UT (T0=60727.14903935 [MJD]) with the position 59.477, -15.139 (uncertainty of 3 arcmin) (GCN 39396). The peak count rate was ~2200 counts/sec (15-350 keV), at ~0 sec after the trigger. REM 60cm robotic telescope at the ESO observatory detected an optical counterpart 70s after T0 (60727.14984954 MJD) in r = 16.5 +/- 0.2 (GCN 39406). Ongoing, the optical afterglow was detected by the following teams in chronological order: DDRAGO (GCN 39397), REM (GCN 39406), GRANDMA/TAROT (GCN 39417), 1.6m Mephisto (GCN 39412), Mondy (GCN 39424), Assy (GCN 39422), NOT (GCN 39413), LCO (GCN 39425), TNOT (GCN 39446). The possible rebrightening to ~20 mag was reported by one team with two instruments (GCN 39426, GCN 39427) at T+1.4 days (60728.54903935 MJD), but was not confirmed by others. A common redshift of z=0.768 was found by VLT/X-shooter at the position of the afterglow trace ~22.5h after T0 (60728.08653935 MJD). However, no clear emission or absorption features are detected. The X-ray burst emission was detected by the Konus-Wind (GCN 39423) at T+4.4 s (60727.14909028 MJD) and X-ray afterglow by EP-FXT (GCN 39491) at T+2.1 days (60729.24903935 MJD) at the enhanced Swift_XRT position (39404). The radio afterglow was detected by VLA at the centre frequency of 10 GHz (X-band), bandwidth of 4 GHz at T+1.95 days (60729.09903935 MJD), and by ATCA (GCN 39501) at the enhanced Swift-XRT (GCN 39404) position at T+2.2 days (60729.34903935 MJD), with no detection at the initial Swift-XRT position (GCN 39396) at T+6 minutes (60727.15320602 MJD). Swift released refined analysis circulars for the XRT and BAT instruments 1-2 days after the initial trigger (T0). The first XRT refined analysis occurred approximately 600s after the burst, while the BAT detection was refined around 18 hours post-trigger (GCN 39414, GCN 39471). The final BAT analysis yielded a T90 duration of 1.80 +/- 0.32 seconds in the 15-350 keV band.

GRB 241025A **long and high redshift** discovered by **SWIFT/BAT** at 2024-10-25T01:36:50 UT (T0 is defined as the Swift trigger) is a long GRB (T90=180s in the 15-350 keV), GCN 37859. The GRB was independently detected by other experiments as **Konus-Wind** on 2024-10-25T01:36:26 with a duration of about 140s in the 20-300 keV (GCN 37927), **VZLUSAT-2** about 63s on 2024-10-25 01:36:50 UTC in the 60 - 1700 keV (GCN 38162), **Fermi/GBM** on 2024-10-25T01:36:26 of T90 of 124 s (50-300 keV  (GCN 37860, 37886), **SVOM/GRM** on 2024-10-25T01:36:40 with T90 of 37.6 +1.7/-1.1 s in the 15 - 5000 keV (GCN 37863), **EP/WXT** on 2024-10-25T01:35:29 with T90 of about 300s in the 0.5-4.0 keV (GCN 37864,37872). The X-ray counterpart was found by **Swift/XRT** (GCN 37868, GCN 37888) and **EP/FXT** (at the same location). A optical follow-up campaign was performed including SVOM/UVOT (only in white filter, GCN 37919) **TRT** (GCN 37862), **DDOTI** (GCN 37865), **SVOM/VT** (GCN 37871), **GRANDMA and KNC** (GCN 37882,37926,38298 including VIRT and TNOT), **GROWTH-India** Telescope (GCN 37890), **Konkoly** (GCN 37891), **DFOT** (GCN 37893), **Mondy** (GCN 37912), **SAO RAS** (GCN 37914, 37923), **LBT** (GCN 38114), **COLIBRI** (GCN 37889) The redshift was measured by **NOT** (GCN 37866). Radio observations were also performed with VLA (GCN 38130). The coordinates of the Skyportal page of the ones provided by the detection of the afterglow optical counterpart of Swift/UVOT

**GRB 251222A** (also associated with **EP251222b** ) was triggered by **SVOM/ECLAIRs** at **2025-12-22T17:05:46** UTC (T0=61031.712337963 is defined as the SVOM trigger) and is a **long GRB** , detected for ** >200 s** in 4–120 keV with multiple peaks (GCN 43516). The burst was independently detected by Fermi/GBM at 2025-12-22 17:05:51.27 UT with **T90 ≈ 83 s** (50–300 keV, GCN 43222). SVOM/GRM triggered at 2025-12-22T17:05:52 UT with **T90 = 85.5 (+3.0/−3.5) s** (15–5000 keV, GCN 43202). Einstein Probe/WXT detected EP251222b with an event starting at 2025-12-22T17:04:52 UT and lasting **~350 s** (0.5–4 keV, GCN 43215). Konus-Wind reported a long burst with total duration **~83 s** and prompt spectral fits (CPL; e.g. time-integrated **Ep ~ 102 keV** ) and derived energetics assuming **z = 3.171** (including **Eiso ≈ 2.21×10^53 erg** ) - GCN 43214. The **X-ray** counterpart was found by **Swift/XRT** (GCN 43191, GCN 43213) at RA, Dec (J2000) = 05:08:46.81, −07:12:48.7. 
A optical follow-up campaign was performed including **SVOM/VT** (GCN 43189,GCN 43203), **NOT** (GCN 43194), **Calapai** (GCN 43195), **DFOT** (GCN 43207, GCN 43224), **LCO** (GCN 43208, GCN 43212), **GOTO** (GCN 43209), **SVOM/COLIBR** (GCN 43225), **ZTSH** (GCN 43226), **KNC** (GCN 43229), **AbAO** (GCN 43230), **FTW** (GCN 43233), **Kinder** (GCN 43236), **NUTTelA-TAO** (GCN 43237), **Mephisto** (GCN 43250), **Mondy** (GCN 43273). The redshift was measured by **VLT/X-shooter** (GCN 43204). Radio observation was performed with **VLA** (GCN 43415).  The coordinates of the Skyportal page of the ones provided by the detection of the afterglow optical counterpart of SVOM/VT. To be confirmed: TAROT, COLIBRI

The Swift Burst Alert Telescope (**BAT**) triggered and located the long GRB (30 duration s in the 15-350 keV range) GRB 241026A on 2024-10-26 at 22:42:32 UT (T0) (GCN 37896,37971). The GRB has also been detected and located by **Fermi/GBM** in the 44-300 keV (T90 16s)  (GCN 37894,37917), by **GECAM** with a T90 = 4.9(+4.8,-3.6) s in the 6-6000 keV range (GCN 37924), by **SVOM/GRM** with a T90 of 18.5 +4.0/-3.7 s in the 15-300 keV range (GCN 37921), and by **GRBAlpha** with a T90 duration of 10 seconds in the 80 - 950 keV range (GCN 37929).**XRT** identified an uncatalogued X-ray source (GCN 37896, 37904, 37908), same as  **EP** (GCN 37909).

The optical follow-up campaign was performed: **UVOT** (non-detection - GCN 37947), **SAO RAS** (detections - GCN 37899, GCN 37953, GCN 38028), **WINTER** (non-detection - GCN 37915), Colibri (detection - GCN 37900), **KAIT** (marginal detection - GCN 37903), **Las Cumbres** (detection - GCN 37913), **GROWTH-India** (detection - GCN 37918), **BTA** and **Zeiss-1000** (detection - GCN 37922), VIRT (non-detection - GCN 38299), **LBT** (detection - GCN 37969). 

*BTA* provided the redshift and was confirmed by LBT.

On GRANDMA side: TNOT (detection - GCN 37928, GCN 38035) detected the afterglow at T0+16.7 hrs and T0+33.7 hrs, as well as KNC-Utah, which found a faint afterglow at 19.91 +/- 0.17 mag and a limit of 20.29 mag in Rc and TRT, which marginally detected the afterglow. VLA detected a radio source at T0+4.05 days with central frequencies of 6, 10, and 15 GHz. Redshift is found to be 2.79 (GCN 37916 and GCN 37925). The coordinates in Skyportal are from SAO-RAS (GCN 37899).
